title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
summary_zh: 本文开发了一种基于第一原理的机器学习力场，用于聚合物模拟。方法上，仅使用量子化学计算训练力场，预测了多种聚合物的宏观性质。实验表明，该力场在预测聚合物密度方面与经典力场相当或更准确。
summary_en: This paper develops a machine learning force field derived from first principles for polymer simulation. The method trains the force field using quantum-chemical calculations alone, predicting bulk properties across a range of polymers. Experiments show that this force field is as accurate or more accurate in predicting polymer densities than established classical force fields.
insights: 创新点：基于第一原理开发机器学习力场
方法亮点：仅使用量子化学计算训练力场
关键发现：力场在预测聚合物密度方面表现优异
insights_en: Novelty: Developing a machine learning force field based on first principles
Method highlight: Training the force field using only quantum-chemical calculations
Key finding: The force field excels in predicting polymer densities
abstract: Polymers are a versatile class of materials with widespread industrial applications. Advanced computational tools could revolutionize their design, but the complex, multi-scale nature of polymers poses significant modeling challenges. Classical force fields often lack the accuracy and transferability that polymers demand, while quantum-chemical methods are prohibitively expensive for the large systems and long timescales involved. Here we develop a fast, scalable machine learning force field and show that, trained on quantum-chemical calculations alone, without any experimental data, it predicts measured bulk properties across a broad range of polymers. It reproduces polymer densities as accurately as, or better than, established classical force fields and captures the glass transition signature in the density-temperature curve, enabling the prediction of glass transition temperatures. To accelerate progress in this domain, we release a benchmark of experimental bulk properties for 130 polymers and an accompanying quantum-chemical dataset, laying the foundation for a fully in silico design pipeline for next-generation polymeric materials. The authors develop a machine learning force field trained only on quantum-chemical data that can reproduce measured key polymer properties such as densities and glass transition temperatures.

title: AnyNav: Visual neuro-symbolic friction learning for off-road navigation
summary_zh: 研究越野导航问题。提出基于神经符号的视觉摩擦估计和导航框架。结合视觉感知和物理模型。
summary_en: Studies off-road navigation. Introduces a vision-based friction estimation and navigation framework grounded in neuro-symbolic principles. Integrates visual perception with a physical model.
insights: 创新点：结合视觉感知和物理模型
方法亮点：神经符号方法应用于导航
关键发现：提高导航在复杂环境中的泛化能力
insights_en: Novelty: Integrates visual perception with a physical model
Method highlight: Applies neuro-symbolic methods to navigation
Key finding: Improves navigation generalization in complex environments
abstract: Off-road navigation is critical for a wide range of field robotics applications from planetary exploration to disaster response. However, it remains a longstanding challenge due to unstructured environments and the inherently complex terrain–vehicle interactions. Traditional physics-based methods struggle to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics underlying these interactions, while purely data-driven approaches often overfit to specific motion patterns, vehicle geometries, or platforms, limiting their generalization in diverse, real-world scenarios. To address these limitations, we introduce AnyNav, a vision-based friction estimation and navigation framework grounded in neuro-symbolic principles. Our approach integrates neural networks for visual perception with symbolic physical models for reasoning about terrain-vehicle dynamics. To enable learning in a self-supervised manner for real-world settings, we adopt the imperative learning paradigm, where a bilevel optimization framework leverages physics-based optimization for training the friction network. This explicit incorporation of physical reasoning substantially improves generalization across terrains, vehicle types, and operating conditions. Leveraging the predicted friction coefficients, we further develop a physics-informed navigation system capable of generating physically feasible, time-efficient paths together with corresponding speed profiles. We demonstrate that AnyNav seamlessly transfers from simulation to real-world robotic platforms, exhibiting strong robustness across different four-wheeled vehicles and diverse off-road environments.

title: Odyssey: An automotive lidar-inertial odometry dataset with GNSS-denied situations
summary_zh: 本文提出Odyssey数据集，用于LIO和SLAM系统评估。数据集包含长时间GNSS拒绝环境下的LIO数据，弥补了现有数据集的不足。
summary_en: This paper presents the Odyssey dataset for evaluating LIO and SLAM systems. The dataset contains LIO data under prolonged GNSS-denied situations, addressing the limitations of existing datasets.
insights: 创新点：提出Odyssey数据集，解决GNSS拒绝环境下的LIO评估问题。
方法亮点：提供长时间GNSS拒绝环境下的LIO数据。
关键发现：数据集弥补了现有数据集的不足。
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes the Odyssey dataset to address LIO evaluation under GNSS-denied situations.
Method highlight: Provides LIO data under prolonged GNSS-denied situations.
Key finding: The dataset addresses the limitations of existing datasets.
abstract: The development and evaluation of Lidar-Inertial Odometry (LIO) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems require a precise reference trajectory. The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is often used as a foundation for this, but its signals can be unreliable in obstructed environments due to multi-path effects or loss-of-signal. While existing datasets compensate for sporadic GNSS loss by incorporating Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) measurements, the commonly used systems do not permit prolonged study of GNSS-denied environments due to accumulated drift. Consequently, existing automotive benchmarks are typically restricted to short GNSS-denied segments. To close this gap, we present Odyssey, an automotive LIO dataset featuring: (1) prolonged, previously unseen GNSS-denied environments with reference trajectories enabled by a navigation-grade Ring Laser Gyroscope (RLG)-based RTK/INS; (2) a large and diverse collection of 36 sequences that range from rural outdoor environments to urban and indoor scenarios; and (3) experimentally validated uncertainties, allowing for precise quantification of reference error. Besides providing data for LIO, Odyssey also supports place recognition tasks through threefold trajectory repetition and integration of external mapping data via precise geodetic coordinates. All data, dataloader and supplementary material are available online at https://odyssey.uni-goettingen.de/ .

title: Spontaneous gas film expansion at an oil–water interface
summary_zh: 研究揭示了油水界面自发形成气膜的现象。方法上，通过微结构限制和气泡引入，实现气膜形成。实验表明，气膜的形成降低了局部压力，促进了溶解空气的吸收。
summary_en: This study reveals the spontaneous formation of a gas film at an oil-water interface. The method involves microstructural confinement and bubble introduction to achieve gas film formation. Experiments show that the formation of the gas film lowers local pressure, promoting the uptake of dissolved air.
insights: 创新点：揭示油水界面自发形成气膜的现象
方法亮点：微结构限制和气泡引入实现气膜形成
关键发现：气膜的形成降低了局部压力，促进了溶解空气的吸收
insights_en: Novelty: Revealing the spontaneous formation of a gas film at an oil-water interface
Method highlight: Microstructural confinement and bubble introduction to achieve gas film formation
Key finding: The formation of the gas film lowers local pressure, promoting the uptake of dissolved air
abstract: Spontaneous interfacial separation of oil and water, by inserting a gas film between the two liquids, is thermodynamically unfavorable because the oil–water interface is replaced by oil–gas and water–gas interfaces with a higher combined interfacial energy. Here, we demonstrate that microstructural confinement enables this transition after bubble introduction through the coupling of wetting, capillarity, and gas transport. Spontaneous oil imbibition into a water-submerged micropillar array, together with local contact-line pinning, deforms the oil–water interface into a metastable meniscus and generates a local pressure deficit in the confined oil. This deficit, combined with the bubble’s interfacial configuration, lowers its air partial pressure and promotes dissolved-air uptake from the surrounding water. Geometric confinement, reduced oil pressure, and low oil–gas interfacial tension favor bubble lateral invasion of adjacent oil-filled cells over vertical extrusion. As the gas front advances, meniscus relaxation and oil redistribution promote further wetting, renewing the capillary conditions that support gas film propagation. We develop a coupled transport-capillarity framework that captures these morphological transitions and predicts a characteristic timescale for gas film evolution, determined by the interaction among geometry, capillarity, and gas-phase transport. Spatially varying the microstructure further controls the propagation pathway and morphology of the gas film. These findings show how favorable wetting can support an energetically costly interfacial transformation through a confinement-induced capillary pressure field, providing a general mechanism for gas-mediated separation in confined multiphase systems.

title: Compliant residual DAgger: Improving real-world contact-rich manipulation with human corrections
summary_zh: 研究数据聚合挑战。引入CR-DAgger，提高接触丰富操作性能。
summary_en: Studies challenges in Dataset Aggregation. Introduces CR-DAgger to enhance performance on contact-rich manipulation tasks.
insights: 方法亮点：合规干预接口
abstract: We address key challenges in Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) for real-world contact-rich manipulation: how to collect informative human correction data and how to effectively update policies with this new data. We introduce Compliant Residual DAgger (CR-DAgger), which contains two novel components: (1) a Compliant Intervention Interface that leverages compliance control, allowing humans to provide gentle, accurate delta action corrections without interrupting the ongoing robot policy execution; and (2) a Compliant Residual Policy formulation that learns from human corrections while incorporating force feedback and force control. Our system significantly enhances performance on precise contact-rich manipulation tasks using minimal correction data, improving base policy success rates by 64% on four challenging tasks (book flipping, belt assembly, cable routing, and gear insertion) while outperforming both retraining-from-scratch and finetuning approaches. Through extensive real-world experiments, we provide practical guidance for implementing effective DAgger in real-world robot learning tasks. Result videos are available at: https://compliant-residual-dagger.github.io/ .

title: MariSense: A multi-modal dataset for environmental perception in maritime autonomy
summary_zh: 本文提出MariSense数据集，用于海上自主导航的环境感知研究。数据集包含多模态数据，如毫米波雷达，以应对海上感知挑战。
summary_en: This paper presents the MariSense dataset for environmental perception research in maritime autonomy. The dataset includes multi-modal data, such as mmWave radar, to address maritime perception challenges.
insights: 创新点：提出MariSense数据集，应对海上感知挑战。
方法亮点：整合多模态数据，如毫米波雷达。
关键发现：数据集有助于海上自主导航研究。
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes the MariSense dataset to address maritime perception challenges.
Method highlight: Integrates multi-modal data, such as mmWave radar.
Key finding: The dataset aids in maritime autonomy research.
abstract: Maritime autonomous navigation enables unmanned surface vehicles to perform multiple tasks and can also serve as a driver-assistance system for manned vessels, improving safety and comfort. Compared with on-road scenes, maritime perception faces unique challenges: optical sensors degrade due to reflections and sea fog, while wind and waves cause large platform motions that disrupt perception stability. Therefore, high-quality multi-modal datasets are crucial. Meanwhile, 4D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has been successfully applied in on-road scenes due to its all-weather, all-day, and high-resolution sensing capabilities, but its maritime characteristics and waveform design effects remain underexplored. To address these challenges, we present MariSense, a multi-modal dataset for maritime autonomy perception. MariSense is the first to introduce the concept of dynamic waveform 4D mmWave radar into maritime scenes, integrating multi-waveform radars with visible and thermal cameras, LiDAR, marine radar, Automatic Identification System (AIS), and navigation sensors, all with extrinsic calibration. The dataset covers various scenes such as anchorages and fairways under varying weather, time, and sea conditions. We establish benchmarks for object detection, tracking, and odometry, and evaluate baseline methods, highlighting the need for improved maritime perception, multi-modal fusion, and adaptive 4D mmWave radar waveform design. The dataset can be downloaded from https://github.com/ORCAUBOAT/MariSense .
